newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cricket-New South Wales humbled by Western Australia.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cricket-New South Wales humbled by Western Australia.

text.p: New South Wales surrendered their last seven wickets for just four runs to be all out for 89 on the first day of their Sheffield Shield match against Western Australia at the WACA ground on Friday.

Off-spinner Bret Mulder took five of the last six wickets to fall to finish with five wickets for two runs from six remarkable overs. Mulder, 33, returned to the Western Australia team after an absence of eight years.
New South Wales had earlier struggled to 52 for three before their dismal collapse gave Western Australia the chance to extend their lead at the top of the Shield standings.
Opener Corey Richardson top-scored with 28. The extras total of six was superior to the scores of six New South Wales batsmen.
Third-placed New South Wales now have virtually no chance of saving the match, which they need to win to have any chance of reaching the Shield final later this month.
In Adelaide, Victoria played strongly to bowl out last-placed South Australia for 216 on the first day of their match at the Adelaide Oval.
Damien Fleming, David Saker and Ian Harvey took three wickets each in a poor batting display by South Australia.
Opener Ben Johnson offered the most resistance, scoring 46.

In Hobart, axed Australia batsman Ricky Ponting kept alive his hopes of winning a place on the Ashes tour of England later this year with an unbeaten century for Tasmania on the first day of their match against Queensland.
Tasmania had been in early trouble at 31 for three before Ponting's innings of 116 not helped his side recover to 193 for four at tea.
